problems.reason: Both sentences state that David Gillette concluded Dystrophaeus was a member of the Diplodocidae.

The classification of Dystrophaeus is inconsistent: Gillette (15,21) places it in Diplodocidae, while other analyses (17,19) argue against diplodocid affinity, and 20 and 22 place it in Dicraeosauridae.
Sentence 8 refers to receiving the fossils from Joseph Leidy, but no prior mention of Leidy or the context of the receipt.
Sentences 4 and 5 discuss the etymology of the genus and species names, which is about the naming rather than the animal’s biology.
